verdicts.correction: The .err pins COBOLNET0899, which is the 'recognized but not implemented' code (DiagnosticCatalog: ReportGenerateNeedsControl is declared under NotImplemented). That code means a compiler limitation, not an SR2 violation, so the golden asserts the known kb/Work PB1028 defect as expected behaviour and breaks when PB1028 re-codes it. The program itself is correct: it is otherwise legal, and reject-at 85 2002 2014 2023 is right. Fix: change the .err to the SR2-specific message substring only, 'the report-name form requires a CONTROL clause' (the compiler's actual output is 'error COBOLNET0899: GENERATE R-1: the report-name form requires a CONTROL clause in the report description entry (ISO §14.9.16.3 SR2)'). Or hold the golden until PB1028 assigns a syntax-rule code.

all_upheld_flag: Not all upheld: 1 of 11 was overturned. GR-13.18.27.4-3 is suspected-defect and was not judged. For each golden I derived stdout from the spec before reading the .out. GENERATE: from §14.9.16.4 GR2/4/5 and §14.9.46.4 GR3 (CH1 on the first GENERATE with no detail, a break giving CF then CH2, a no-break summary GENERATE printing nothing, TERMINATE giving the final CF), which matches. A detail-printing summary GENERATE would add [DE1] or [DE2], so the golden pins GR2. GROUP INDICATE: from §13.18.28.4 GR1 a)/c). The blank columns follow from absolute COLUMN positions. The bare 'GROUP' spelling is pinned because HDR would otherwise appear on lines 2 and 4. ACCESS: I checked READ SR8/SR9, which make READ RLD with INVALID KEY in dynamic mode a random read. I also checked the READ GR25 relative-key update, WRITE GR42 a) status 21 for IY, alternate-key order C1/B2/A3 after START, random INVALID KEY 23, and dynamic random-then-NEXT positioning. A random-assuming implementation would print R9 first for RL, so GR1 is pinned. Hex: I checked every value against the CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-95/97 text (ORD = code+1, LENGTH, code-unit comparison, U+FFFD on DISPLAY). I ran cite.py --check on every § in all headers, including 14.9.30.4 25), 14.9.51.4 29)/42), 9.1.13.5 3) a) and 15.70.4 1)/2), and all were OK. Caveats I noted but did not overturn on: (1) the 85 GENERATE golden uses X"0A"/X"0D"/X"0C". Historically, hex alphanumeric literals are a 2002 addition, but Annex E covers only 2014->2023, so ISO 2023 cannot settle this. constructs.json does not gate them, and 8 existing tests/conformance/85 report goldens use the same byte-wise read-back. (2) The report read-back assumes a text/LF physical file layout with no trailing padding. That is implementor-defined but it is the established corpus convention.
